READABILITY.evidence: Module and function docstrings are good, but the business logic uses single-letter names throughout: `v = normalize(value)`, `n = name.lower()`, and `s`, `i`, `j`, `k`, `q` in parse_attrs. The `WS` and `for_search` names are terse, and sanitize_tags has confusing offset arithmetic with no comments.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: Policy sits in named constants and the code is split into helpers, but sanitize_tags is long and has redundant code: `if not quote_aware: off = start`, and `body`/`off` are assigned the same way in both branches. The quoted and unquoted value parsing is duplicated, and the dual-pass loop is hard to change.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: Handles a missing argv with a usage message, reads and writes bytes with an explicit utf-8/surrogateescape encoding, and catches specific exceptions in _chr. The loop counts are magic numbers (`range(5)`, `range(50)`), and `_chr` silently returns "" on an invalid escape.

C6-01-CASE1.evidence: General rules cover the listed classes: any `on*` attribute in any case, srcdoc, and a scheme regex applied after repeated entity, control-character and CSS-escape decoding. Non-image data: URLs are dropped, embedding tags (iframe/object/embed/base) are stripped, SVG attributeName and meta refresh are checked, and malformed or unclosed script tags are removed in a loop.

C6-01-CASE2.evidence: Edits are made in place on the source text and only the offending attribute span is cut. But it over-removes: any `data:` in any attribute value, `javascript:` in a title, and a whole `<style>` emptied for one `@import`. The hidden test_clean_html_unchanged failed, so benign content does get altered.
